specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: 6. Authorization is deny-by-default and evaluated on every executable backend boundary. Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary.

- root, system, namespace-owner, database-owner, and other privileged SurrealDB sessions MUST NOT execute ordinary protected-resource flows or count as privacy/isolation proof because privileged users bypass table permissions;

Application authorization remains required for action semantics and capability checks; record-user table/field permissions plus ResourceBroker are the non-bypassable product data boundary, not the only policy layer.

**[LM-RLS-001]** Multi-user workspace isolation MUST use authenticated record-user table/field permissions intersected with ResourceBroker scope. A `viewer` can read but not create/edit LoomBlocks; a `member` can create and edit; an `admin` can delete and manage workspace settings.

**[LM-RLS-002]** Authority tables default to `PERMISSIONS NONE`; every grant is explicit at the database layer and rechecked by ResourceBroker. Privacy proof MUST execute as authenticated record users because root, namespace, database, and other system users bypass record-user table permissions.

For each of the 68 routes in scope.routes, the handler authenticates the caller with authorize_request (resource kind and action per the route's semantics: reads = ResourceAction::Read + fs.read; creates/updates = Update or Create + fs.write; deletes = Delete + fs.write) BEFORE any protected-table access, and every protected-table read and write of that request executes inside state.surreal.with_record_user_scope(ctx.record_user_scope, ...). No route in scope keeps a root-session read or write of a protected table (including root ensure_workspace_exists lookups that disclose existence: authorize workspace read first, then look up under scope).

Least privilege at the database layer: every Loom table these routes touch has explicit record-user PERMISSIONS in schema.surql that admit exactly the owner's grant for that operation (fn::mt120_loom_block_access / fn::mt109_has_workspace_access with the matching action+capability) and nothing broader; tables currently PERMISSIONS NONE that a scoped route needs (loom_folders, loom_folder_members, knowledge_wiki_projections, loom_wiki_overlays, assets, media_asset_tiers, loom_collections + members, loom_ai_suggestions, knowledge_quick_switcher_recents, loom_block_view_fr_outbox) get per-operation predicates; update NONE on loom_canvas_boards / loom_canvas_placements and create/update NONE on loom_canvas_visual_edges get owner predicates; loom_edges select/create/delete admit user tag edges (not only SYSTEM mention edges) through fn::mt120_loom_block_access. Tables no scoped route needs stay PERMISSIONS NONE (LM-RLS-002 default).

Every kernel_event_ledger receipt appended by a scoped Loom write (KNOWLEDGE_LOOM_BLOCK_MUTATED, KNOWLEDGE_LOOM_TAG_MUTATED, folder/wiki/collection/suggestion/quick-switcher/view-definition/canvas viewport receipts) is accepted by a receipt predicate branch that checks $session = $auth.id, fn::mt109_ledger_access and the matching loom access, and carries the session principal as actor (never a System or header-supplied actor). The owner can read these receipts via GET /kernel/events/aggregates/:type/:id; another account reads 0 of them.

Per route family (blocks+pins+metrics, folders, wiki+overlays+bootstrap/drift/fanout, markdown import + asset import, tags+edges, assets+tiers, collections, views+graph+search+visual-debug, quick-switcher, AI jobs+suggestions, canvas viewport/cards/stage-cards/placements/visual-edges, block-view definitions+results, daily journal): (a) owner positive through the real HTTP route returns the success status and the canonical row reflects the change; (b) anonymous (no session headers) returns the constant denial and the canonical row is unchanged; (c) a second account returns the constant denial (or an empty list for list routes, never the other account's rows) and the canonical row is unchanged; (d) for write routes, a same-account read-only (viewer) principal is denied the write (LM-RLS-001 viewer) - if the grant model cannot express a viewer for a table, record that under residual_risks with the table name instead of inventing sharing.

engine_facts: SurrealDB is pinned =3.2.0 (src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml). Facts verified in surrealdb-core-3.2.0 source by the authority matrix:

F1 Table and field permissions are OFF inside a PERMISSIONS predicate (dbs/options.rs:201 new_for_permission_predicate; doc/check.rs:457-470; exec/permission.rs:87-99). Predicates and the fn::* functions they call see every row and field, including fields that are FOR select NONE.

F2 A top-level query issued on a record-user connection DOES enforce field permissions. Never probe a predicate by running `RETURN fn::...` directly as the record user; it reads permission-hidden fields as NONE and lies. Probe inside a predicate instead (e.g. a probe table whose PERMISSIONS FOR select calls the function).

F3 A denied CREATE, UPDATE or DELETE is SILENTLY IGNORED: no row returned, no error (doc/check.rs:457,469 IgnoreError::Ignore). Every record-user write MUST check the returned row (or a follow-up SELECT) and map an empty result to the constant denial; the failure otherwise surfaces later as a field ASSERT 500, an empty 404, or a guard THROW 403.

F4 REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE/UNSET and DEFINE EVENT bodies run with permissions OFF (doc/purge.rs:376,385; doc/event.rs:52,80). Cascades are never blocked by the caller's delete permission, and cascade targets need no delete predicate for the cascade itself.

F5 Session selection: `SurrealStorage::with_record_user_scope(scope, fut)` (src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal.rs:956 @ab618f46) sets a tokio task-local; `with_data_operation` then signs a cloned client in as the record user. Anything outside that scope, INCLUDING work moved into `tokio::spawn`, runs as root. Re-enter the scope inside every spawned future that touches protected tables.
